DAU = distinct players with >= 1 event on the event_date. Installs = players whose first_open falls on the day.

A/B: observational tests and test design

Observational comparisons (not randomised)

Two-proportion z-test (= chi-square 2x2), 95% CI of the difference, Cohen's h. Traffic source compared within Android only.

iOS D1 is — vs Android (p = —, h —); on Android, google-play installs lead (direct) by — (p —). Correlation, not causation.

Sample size for a D1 retention A/B test

Two-sided test, alpha 0.05, power 0.8, baseline = observed D1; run time = 2 x n / installs per day.

Detecting +2 pp needs — players per arm: about — days at the sampled — installs per day. Run on full traffic or test bigger changes.

Data limitations

  • Sampled export: exactly — events per day. Absolute counts describe the sample; rates are reliable.
  • — of players were acquired before the window; cohorts and LTV use installs inside it only.
  • — of new players have no first_open and are excluded from cohorts.
  • Only — purchases and no ad revenue: monetisation figures are directional.
  • Traffic source is confounded with platform (iOS is (direct) only); app_remove exists only on Android and is not used as a churn label.
  • Platform and source comparisons are observational, not causal.

Pipeline, SQL and validation: github.com/VuHongVi/flood-it-game-analytics · every number is a row of powerbi/data/*.csv (kpi_metrics.csv = results/metrics.json).
